authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Sonic acquired five Harley-Davidson dealerships in April 2026, which the company expects to add about $100 million of annualized revenue to its Powersports Segment.
The company recorded impairment charges of approximately $173.8 million in 2025, mainly on indefinite-lived franchise assets in the Franchised Dealerships Segment.
The Board approved a quarterly cash dividend of $0.41 per share, payable January 15, 2027 to holders of record on December 15, 2026.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (P4 overview; P1 describes the same three segments)
business_model.claim: Sonic is one of the largest U.S. automotive retailers. It reports three segments (Franchised Dealerships, EchoPark, Powersports) and operated 108, 18 and 20 stores respectively at the latest quarter-end.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we operated 108 stores in the Franchised Dealerships Segment, 18 stores in the EchoPark Segment and 20 stores in the Powersports Segment.

business_model.claim: The Franchised Dealerships Segment generates most of the revenue: about 85.0% of total revenue in the last full year, against 13.7% for EchoPark and 1.3% for Powersports.
quotes: In 2025, Franchised Dealerships Segment revenue represented approximately 85.0% of total revenue (compared to 83.9% in 2024).

business_model.basis: stated in the F2 income statement; the magnitude comparison is the analyst's reading of the printed figures
business_model.claim: Revenue comes from four main lines. In the latest nine months these were new vehicles 5,204,200, used vehicles 3,980,500, parts/service/collision repair 1,590,100 and F&I 614,100, out of total revenues of 11,611,300 (table in thousands).

business_model.basis: stated in P3; the figures are from the F2 member lines
business_model.claim: Customers are mainly retail consumers. The company says its new-vehicle strategy focuses on retail rather than fleet sales, and fleet new vehicle revenue is small next to retail new vehicle revenue (65,800 vs 5,138,400, table in thousands, latest nine months).
quotes: Our new vehicle sales strategy focuses on our retail new vehicle sales (as opposed to fleet new vehicle sales)

business_model.claim: New vehicle sales are the largest revenue component and feed the higher-margin businesses. The new vehicle mix is mostly luxury and mid-line import brands, about 86% of new vehicle revenue in the last full year.
quotes: New vehicle sales are the largest component of our total revenue and lead to sales of higher-margin products and services such as finance, insurance, vehicle protection products and other aftermarket products, and parts and service operations.
approximately 86% of our total new vehicle revenue was generated by luxury and mid-line import dealerships

business_model.claim: The company earns F&I income as commissions and fees for arranging third-party financing, warranties, service contracts and insurance, not by providing these products itself.
quotes: Each sale of a new or used vehicle gives us an opportunity to provide our guests with third-party financing and insurance options and earn financing fees and insurance and other aftermarket product commissions.

business_model.claim: Same-store F&I gross profit per retail unit in the franchised segment was $2,630 in the latest quarter, up 2%.
quotes: Same store F&I gross profit per retail unit increased $63 per unit, or 2%, to $2,630 per unit during the three months ended September 30, 2026

business_model.claim: Fixed Operations (parts, service, collision repair) is a steadier, higher-margin business. Same-store Fixed Operations revenue grew 1% in the latest quarter and 3% over nine months, with gross margin of 51.4% in the quarter.
quotes: Our Fixed Operations sales carry a higher gross margin than new and used vehicle sales and generally are not as sensitive to economic conditions as new or used vehicle sales.
driven primarily by increased service capacity as a result of additional technician headcount, and higher parts and labor costs that were passed along to consumers

business_model.claim: EchoPark sells used vehicles through pre-owned specialty retail stores and arranges F&I, with no customer-facing repair services. Its latest-quarter revenue was $596.0 million, up 14%, on 22% higher retail used unit volume. Segment income was $2.0 million, down from $2.6 million a year earlier.
quotes: The EchoPark Segment sells used cars and light trucks and arranges third-party F&I product sales for our guests in pre-owned vehicle specialty retail locations and does not offer customer-facing Fixed Operations services.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 and P8; the annualized revenue figure is a company expectation
business_model.claim: The Powersports Segment sells new and used motorcycles, personal watercraft and all-terrain vehicles, plus service and F&I. It is small (1.3% of revenue in the last full year) but growing by acquisition: five Harley-Davidson dealerships bought in April are expected to add about $100 million of annualized revenue.
quotes: is expected to add approximately $100 million in annualized revenue to Sonic's Powersports Segment

business_model.claim: Franchised-segment new vehicle revenue is driven by unit volume and gross profit per unit. Same-store retail new vehicle revenue fell 7% in the latest quarter on a 7% drop in units, and new vehicle days' supply rose to 65 from 51.
quotes: Same store retail new vehicle revenue decreased 7% during the three months ended September 30, 2026, driven by a 7% decrease in retail new vehicle unit sales volume.

business_model.basis: stated in P6; the figures are from F2
business_model.claim: Segment mix shifts offset each other. The CEO says growth in EchoPark and Powersports offset declines in Franchised Dealerships. Latest-quarter revenue was 3,988,800 against 3,973,800 a year earlier, while net income was 41,100 against 46,800 (table in thousands).
quotes: revenue and gross profit growth in our EchoPark and Powersports segments offset declines in our Franchised Dealerships segment

business_model.basis: stated in F2 and P6; the 75.6% figure is printed in P6
business_model.claim: The largest operating cost is SG&A. In the latest quarter SG&A of 466,800 against gross profit of 617,500 (table in thousands) was 75.6% of gross profit. Management treats SG&A as a percent of gross profit as a key control metric.
quotes: Focus on controllable selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses to maintain structural improvement in SG&A leverage as a percent of gross profit

business_model.basis: stated in P2; the figures are from F1 and F2
business_model.claim: Inventory is largely financed with floor plan borrowings, so interest cost is a direct cost of carrying vehicles. Floor plan interest expense was 64,700 in the latest nine months against 62,200 a year earlier. Floor plan non-trade notes payable were 2,076,800 against inventories of 2,443,000 (table in thousands).
quotes: Floor Plan Financing arrangements allow us to borrow money to buy a particular new vehicle from the manufacturer or a used vehicle on trade-in or at auction and pay off the loan when we sell that particular vehicle.

business_model.claim: The franchise model depends on manufacturers. Each dealership operates under a franchise agreement, and without it the company cannot obtain new vehicles or act as an authorized factory service center.
quotes: Without a franchise or dealer agreement, we cannot obtain new vehicles from a manufacturer or advertise as an authorized factory service center.

competitive_position.basis: stated by the CEO in P6

competitive_position.claim: Fixed Operations (parts, service, collision repair) is a steadier, higher-margin profit source: same-store revenue grew 1% in the quarter and 3% over nine months, and same-store gross margin was 51.4% in the quarter.

Our Fixed Operations sales carry a higher gross margin than new and used vehicle sales and generally are not as sensitive to economic conditions as new or used vehicle sales.

competitive_position.claim: The brand mix is tilted to luxury and mid-line import brands, which the company says have higher operating margins and more stable service departments.
quotes: For 2025, approximately 86% of our total new vehicle revenue was generated by luxury and mid-line import dealerships, which typically have higher operating margins, more stable Fixed Operations departments, lower associate turnover and lower inventory levels than other brand categories.

competitive_position.claim: Manufacturer dependence is a named threat: new vehicle sales are concentrated in luxury and mid-line import brands, and the company is significantly dependent on manufacturer relationships.
quotes: Our new vehicle sales operations are comprised primarily of luxury and mid-line import brands, which exposes us to manufacturer concentration risks.
As a result, we are significantly dependent on our relationships with the manufacturers.
